summary.headline: Suyog Telematics Q4 FY26 revenue INR221 crore, EBITDA margin ~74%, PAT ~30%; Vodafone 5,000-tenancy order expected by June-end drives FY27 plan.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR221 crore, EBITDA of INR1,642 million (about 74% margin), PAT of INR833 million and net profit of INR631 million, with revenue per tower at about INR31,080. Growth was described as about 18% QoQ, driven mainly by Airtel upgrades and BSNL billing starting on about 120-125 previously unbilled sites. FY27 expectations hinge on a Vodafone order (about 5,000 tenancies, around 4,000 towers) that management said should arrive by June-end, while BSNL orders remain unconfirmed pending Tejas network fixes. Management did not finalise funding or a detailed capex plan, deferring both until the Vodafone order is confirmed, and several guidance points were revised or left open.

margin described as improved; Q4 margin expansion attributed to Ind AS 116 reclassification of Monorail govt rent
described as sustained year on year
up from about INR29,000 in the prior year

financial_highlights.value: Loan interest about 9%; total interest up sharply
financial_highlights.change: increase attributed mainly to Ind AS 116 ROU liabilities

segments.name: Tower (IP-1) business
segments.commentary: 6,008 towers carrying 7,318 tenancies across 26 states/UTs, including 4,000+ small cells (1,000+ government sites). Customer mix: Bharti Airtel 48%, Vodafone Idea 26.7%, Jio 22.8%, BSNL 2.5% of revenue.

segments.name: Fiber
segments.commentary: About 6,300 km of aerial fiber; management said fiber revenue in FY27 will be under 2-3% of revenue and expects a larger contribution in FY28-FY29. Fiber is billed on a recurring monthly basis.

segments.name: Lotus Tele Infra (acquired FY26)
segments.commentary: Management said growth is strong but profit is not yet visible due to Ind AS 116 depreciation and interest on 10+ year leases; cited a top line of about INR30 crore and a bottom line of about 30%, with no loan taken.

segments.name: CCTV
segments.commentary: Described as an acquisition tactic to secure non-movable sites; no financial figures given.

guidance_outlook: Vodafone: management expects about 5,000 tenancies (around 4,000 towers) in FY27, with the bulk order expected by June-end or July; deployment to complete within FY27, weighted to Q3 and Q4 with Q2 weak due to monsoon.
Q1 FY27 revenue expected to be similar to Q4 FY26 run-rate; no major growth in Q1.
FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15-20%; full benefit of FY27 rollout expected in FY28.
Revenue per tower expected to stay at INR31,000-32,000 in FY27; BSNL rollout could reduce it by INR1,000-2,000 due to lower pass-through rentals.
FY27 exit tenancies estimated at 12,000-13,000 (7,000 existing plus 5,000 from Vodafone), down from the earlier 17,000 cited on the last call; BSNL excluded until confirmed.

Capex about INR12 lakh per 40m GBT tower; total FY27 capex about INR600 crore for 5,000 towers, with about 50% from internal accruals and existing debt limits and the balance to be financed once the order is final.
Funding plan and final tenancy target to be detailed at the Q1 FY27 call.
capex_capacity: Vodafone 5,000-tenancy rollout planned for FY27 at about INR12 lakh per 40m GBT tower (about INR600 crore total); rollout time about 45-60 days per ground-based tower and 21-30 days per RTT tower.
Management said it can execute 10,000-12,000 new towers a year; existing capacity can absorb about 3,000 sites on internal accruals plus existing debt limits.
BSNL indicated around 30,000 sites in FY27, but no order is confirmed; BSNL sites billed so far total about 1,800 over two years, of which 189 are still pending billing.
Management plans to focus on 10 states, including Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
Acquisitions: management is evaluating smaller IP companies, to be funded from internal accruals; no target finalised.
demand_pricing: Vodafone MSA is pan-India with no tender; allocation expected directly, and management said Vodafone wants only 2-3 IP companies (Indus expected to take the largest share, Suyog next).
BSNL rentals are low: about INR7,000 per site per month versus INR15,000-25,000 from private operators, which lowers revenue per tower when BSNL sites are added.
Revenue per tower gains from technology upgrades of about INR3,000-3,500 per upgrade (Airtel upgrades contributed most of recent growth).
Data centre business: no progress; management said Jio has paused capex until its IPO and Airtel is not doing major capex.
Gross margin per tower stated at 85%; site rentals of about INR20,000 per month in metros (RTT) and INR7,000-10,000 in rural areas are reimbursed by operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund and gear up for Vodafone and BSNL capacity, and what debt is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan yet; funding (internal accruals, debt or equity) to be decided once the Vodafone order is final, with details promised at the Q1 call. Management said the company has enough funds for about 3,000 sites from internal accruals plus existing debt limits.

qa_highlights.question: Is Vodafone's rollout confirmed, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Vodafone has verbally assured a big rollout and direct allocation under the MSA; the bulk order is expected by June-end. Management expects Q2 to be weak due to monsoon, with major numbers in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BSNL revenue only 2.5% despite large rollouts?
qa_highlights.answer: BSNL pays low pass-through rentals (about INR7,000 per site versus INR15,000-25,000 for private operators), so top line per site is lower while PAT percentage is unchanged. No BSNL order is factored in until Tejas network issues are resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Q4 revenue growth come from BSNL billing, Airtel upgrades or new towers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% of the quarter's growth came from BSNL billing on about 120-125 sites; the balance came mainly from Airtel upgrades and early Vodafone rollout.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the interest cost increase and Q4 EBITDA margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely Ind AS 116: ROU lease liabilities lift interest and depreciation, and Monorail's contract renewal for 10 years moved government rent out of COGS, lifting EBITDA margin. Loan interest is about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR600 crore Vodafone capex is debt versus internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% from internal accruals and existing debt limits; the balance to be determined after the final Vodafone order is known.

risks_watch: Vodafone order timing has already slipped from February-March to June-end; a further delay would push FY27 tenancy additions and revenue.
FY27 tenancy target was cut from about 17,000 exit tenancies to 12,000-13,000 within one quarter; BSNL upside is excluded until confirmed.
BSNL orders remain unconfirmed due to Tejas network issues (SIM latching, backhaul stability).
Funding for about INR600 crore Vodafone capex is undecided; the balance beyond about 50% internal funds is open, and debt levels could rise.
Auditor flagged internal controls (rent payment, billing automation, warehouse management); remediation is ongoing.
Ind AS 116 lease accounting is distorting reported EBITDA margin and interest, with Lotus Tele Infra profit not yet visible.
Management said billing for electricity (EB) would be added to top line for account compliance in the current quarter, which may affect reported revenue comparability.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Vodafone and BSNL pipeline, but evasive on timing, funding and BSNL specifics, repeatedly deferring numbers to the Q1 call. Guidance was revised down during the call (tenancies) while the company stated nothing had gone wrong.
